channel.title: ESAHubble Images
channel.description: The ESAHubble Images feed showcases breathtaking images and scientific observations captured by the NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope. Explore stunning infrared views of nebulae, star-forming regions, and isolated planetary-mass objects, accompanied by detailed descriptions and insights into the latest astronomical discoveries.

item.title: Cat’s Head Nebula (Hubble WFC3, Webb NIRCam, and Webb MIRI images)
item.description:
The NASA/ESA Hubble and the NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescopes recently stared at an eerie star-forming scene within the Carina Nebula, a massive gas and dust cloud located approximately 7,500 light-years away from Earth. The two telescopes offer complementary views of the shadowy form, nicknamed the Cat’s Head Nebula, which reflects the “magical” process of star formation. Hubble’s visible-light view shows the cat as a dark, elongated dust pillar and hints of young forming stars, while Webb’s infrared-light imagery unveils many stars and other hidden details. 

This collage shows three views of the Cat’s Head Nebula. Left: in visible light from Hubble’s WFC3 instrument; centre: in near-infrared from Webb’s NIRCam instrument; right: in mid-infrared from Webb’s MIRI instrument.

[Image description: A collage of three images of the Cat’s Head Nebula. On the right is a Hubble visible-light image. A dark brown, opaque filament of dust is in the center, stretching from the bottom to almost the very top. It has a narrow, irregular shape that resembles a cat sitting with its back toward the viewer and a tail extending downward. In the centre is Webb’s NIRCam view where bright red spot marks the eye. The top half of the background is bright blue. Approximately halfway down, cutting diagonally across the frame, the background colour changes from blue to yellow, orange, and finally red near the bottom. On the right is Webb’s MIRI view. A bluish-gray filament of dust is in the center, stretching from the bottom to almost the very top. It has a narrow, irregular shape that resembles a cat sitting with its back toward the viewer and a tail extending downward.]

item.title: Cat’s Head Nebula (Webb NIRCam image)
item.description:
The NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope’s near-infrared image of the Cat’s Head Nebula peers through some of the dust to reveal a dense field of stars and the filament’s complex surface structure. Faint, wispy structures to the left of the pillar contain material exposed to intense stellar radiation.

Webb captures a dense field of stars, shown in blue and yellow. Even in near-infrared light, some stars are still enshrouded in dust. The bright region marking the cat’s eye may contain an embedded young star. The telescope’s high-resolution imagery even reveals faint background galaxies. 

[Image description: Near-infrared image of the Cat’s Head Nebula by the James Webb Space Telescope. An orange-brown filament of dust is in the center, stretching from the bottom to almost the very top. It has a narrow, irregular shape that resembles a cat sitting with its back toward the viewer and a tail extending downward. The tail ends at the lower one-third of the image and widens to a squarish dust cloud. The cat’s head is turned toward the right, revealing a yellow glowing eye. The background is mostly blue, with the top right corner revealing the black background of space. On the cat’s left are ghostly filaments of dust. Scattered throughout the view are many yellow and blue stars, some with Webb’s signature eight-point diffraction spikes, and a few faint background galaxies.]
